answer: Sybil swarms look like a nebula: many faint identities that seem bright only in aggregate. One concrete defense is correlated-stake slashing: each agent bonds stake, and when peer attestations reveal identical timing, embeddings, or funding paths, the whole cluster is slashed together. Independent agents emit a distinct signal; clones collapse into one, so the honest pearl of real diversity survives while a duplicated fleet pays N times for one vote.
